mechanism_narrative: Sustained elevation in RESIDENTIAL mobility above its pre-pandemic baseline indicates households are consolidating activity at home, which mechanically reduces trips to retail and recreation venues and pushes RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above +10% for all four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in TRANSIT mobility below -30% for two consecutive weeks signals enforced travel restrictions that cut foot traffic to retail districts, causing RETAIL_REC to decline over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -30% and stays there for two consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days even though TRANSIT remains below -30% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM visits climb toward baseline while TRANSIT remains deeply negative, households are shifting from discretionary retail to essential shopping, and this substitution keeps RETAIL_REC depressed over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -5% while TRANSIT falls below -30%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than over the last 14 days when GROCERY_PHARM > -5% and TRANSIT < -30%.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, a sharp week-on-week fall in WORKPLACES mobility signals renewed remote-work mandates that remove office-worker footfall from retail areas, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES falling >5 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility persistently above +10% reflects a home-centric routine that reduces shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC over the next week is lower than its trailing four-week mean.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the next week is higher than its trailing four-week mean while RESIDENTIAL stays above +10%.

mechanism_narrative: A joint drop in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility indicates coordinated policy restrictions on movement; this compound suppression of commuting and transit use lowers retail footfall, pushing RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both fall by more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both drop by >2 points in a week.

mechanism_narrative: In the late-autumn season with active distancing rules, PARKS mobility stuck below -55% signals outdoor recreation is suppressed, and the associated reduced pedestrian flow spills over into lower retail-and-recreation activity over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays below -55% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the next week is higher than its trailing four-week mean while PARKS remains below -55% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for three consecutive weeks and this positive momentum will carry forward, making the next four-week mean higher than the trailing four-week mean.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to its trailing 28-day mean, breaking the three-week upward streak.
